title: Evaluating a Deterministic-Validator Plus Single-Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We study whether a guarded pipeline—an LLM generator followed by a deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first-pass misconfiguration in intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under a preregistered paired design (cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1), we generated 300 deterministic intent tasks and compared (a) single-shot LLM generation (baseline) and (b) the same generation guarded by a deterministic validator with one allowed automated repair (guarded). We used a single hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a frozen validator/repair adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Results: baseline success = 299/300 (99.667%), guarded success = 300/300 (100.0%); absolute paired difference = 0.00333 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.01]); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. The preregistered hypotheses (≥50% relative reduction in fail rate) were not supported. We document a near-ceiling baseline, zero infrastructure failures, and complete reproducible execution artifacts. We discuss operational implications, failure-mode lessons, and threats to internal/construct/external validity. All experimental artifacts, preregistration, and the required Disclosure Statement are archived with the run.

sections.introduction: Intent-driven NetOps proposes translating high-level human intents into low-level device configurations, but LLM-generated artifacts can introduce misconfiguration risks (reachability, connectivity, ordering). Prior work advocates verifier- or simulator-in-the-loop architectures and RAG/validator safety nets to reduce factual errors and misconfiguration (see Related Work). We preregistered and executed a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment to quantify whether a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair iteration meaningfully reduces first-pass misconfiguration relative to single-shot LLM generation on a controlled, paired intent→configuration task set.
sections.related_work: Recent literature demonstrates LLMs can synthesize network configuration templates and translate intent, with RAG and verifier-assisted loops improving grounding in domain QA and other safety-critical tasks [10.1002/nem.2313; 10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1]. Architectural proposals commonly combine LLM generation with deterministic validators/simulators and human approval for safer NetOps workflows [10.1145/3098822.3098834]. Evidence on how much deterministic validators plus automated repair reduce operational misconfiguration rates in reproducible, paired experiments remains sparse; evaluations in adjacent domains indicate hybrid deterministic safety nets reduce hallucination but transfer characteristics depend on corpus, validator fidelity, and task realism [10.2139/ssrn.6608518; 10.36227/techrxiv.176784505.56675782/v1]. NIST and community reviews emphasize characterization of failure modes and adversarial robustness for operational assurance [10.6028/nist.ai.100-2e2023].
sections.methodology: Preregistration: study cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1 (frozen before execution) specified a paired confirmatory design comparing baseline (single LLM generation) vs guarded (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) on N=300 deterministic task seeds. Estimand and hypothesis: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; H1 predicted ≥50% relative reduction in first-pass misconfiguration. Model and adapter: single hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) called via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; validator/repair implementation and task generator were frozen artifacts documented in the preregistration. Task bank: 300 synthetic intent→configuration pairs produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; per-task reference configurations were available for automatic scoring. Execution contract limited to 1 initial generation call per task and at most 1 repair call per task. Primary analysis: exact McNemar paired test (alpha=0.05) on pass/fail outcomes; prespecified sensitivity and multiplicity controls described in the preregistration. All seeds, raw model outputs, validator traces, repair prompts, logs, and artifact hashes were recorded and archived in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution completed without infrastructure failures (planned episodes 600, completed 600, model_calls_used 301). Aggregated per-condition counts: baseline successes = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded successes = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired contingency table: n11 = 299, n10 = 1 (guarded success / baseline fail), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Confirmatory test (exact McNemar two-sided) returned p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.00333; bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). No failed episodes, no missingness under the preregistered treatment (complete_pair_primary). Repair-stage calls occurred once per the execution_log (repair stage count = 1); the single discordant pair was resolved in the guarded arm. Secondary analyses (repair success rate, failure-category stratification) are constrained by the single discordant observation and are therefore inconclusive; full per-task validator traces and repair artifacts are archived.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: the guarded pipeline did not produce a statistically detectable improvement over baseline in this experiment. The primary driver is a near-ceiling baseline pass rate (299/300), leaving minimal room for measurable improvement under the preregistered estimand and planned sample. Operational implication: when LLM single-shot generation already attains very high validity on constrained synthetic tasks, a validator+single-repair design may yield limited measurable benefit; however, the guarded pipeline did deterministically fix the single baseline failure. The result does not falsify the general utility of validators or multi-iteration repair in broader, harder, or adversarial settings. The execution manifest documents deterministic seeding, complete artifacts, and no post-lock human manuscript editing. Recommended next steps: larger and more adversarial task suites, multi-model comparisons, stress tests that exercise validator coverage gaps, multi-iteration repair experiments, and emulation runs that execute configurations against realistic network simulators/emulators to capture semantic/runtime consequences beyond syntactic/constraint validation.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered paired experiment (N=300) testing whether a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair iteration reduces first-pass misconfiguration for gpt-5-mini generated network configurations found no statistically detectable improvement versus single-shot generation because baseline generation was already near-ceiling (299/300). The guarded pipeline did resolve the one observed baseline failure. Future work should evaluate harder, adversarial, and production-representative task banks, extend validator coverage, and measure operational outcomes in emulated execution to better quantify practical safety gains from verifier-assisted agentic NetOps architectures.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor-template scope limit external validity to broad production environments.
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.
Near-ceiling baseline performance (299/300) produced low observable power to detect improvements for the preregistered target effect (50% relative reduction).
Validation here used deterministic configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; runtime execution consequences remain unmeasured.
